ROOM: the shared BEDROOM of two lower-ranking imperial consorts (a Thường tại and a Quý nhân) living together in the West side hall of Chung Túy cung in an ancient Chinese imperial palace, a real bedroom in daily use, modest compared with a high consort's but still pretty and noble: carved and lacquered wood, embroidered silk, never bare or poor. The main subject, like the bed in image 1, is TWO BEDS standing side by side in the middle of the picture, together filling the central half of the width (the left bed's posts well away from the left edge): two smaller carved canopy beds with a low carved partition between them; the first bed hung with pale green gauze curtains tied back, a pale green embroidered quilt and pillows (the Thường tại's rank colour); the second bed hung with pale blue gauze curtains tied back, a pale blue embroidered quilt and pillows (the Quý nhân's rank colour); a low step in front of each. Each girl has her own small dressing corner: a little dressing table with a round bronze mirror, a comb and powder boxes, and a small stool. Around them: a modest painting table with brushes and colour dishes; a folding screen painted with irises; hanging palace lanterns; a small side table with a teapot; a vase of irises, a folded fan, an incense burner, a clothes rack with two robes; dark wood with soft lilac lanterns; a lattice window letting in summer morning light. IMPORTANT: no phoenix anywhere — the canopy frame and furniture are carved only with flowers, leaves and clouds, no phoenix, no dragon, no bird carved on the bed; no imperial yellow and no golden-yellow fabric anywhere: quilt, pillows, throws and curtains are only in pale green, pale blue and ivory white. FLOOR: large smooth polished pale stone tiles visible between the furniture, no large rug or carpet covering the floor (at most a small mat under the bed step); the pair of beds, large and close, clearly the main subject like the bed in image 1, sits in the central half of the width. LIGHT: soft warm morning daylight from the right, like the light on the girl in image 2, so a person standing in the room looks lit by it. Do not leave the room empty like a stage; it should feel natural and furnished, people will simply be placed in it later. LEFT SIDE (owner Lượt 406): the left part of the room near the viewer stays open like in image 1 — only small, low objects there at most, never a large piece of furniture or a big object close up at the left edge, because people will stand on the left. In the left foreground there is only open stone-tiled floor, with at most a low basket or a small pair of slippers; no table, no stool, no vase, no canopy curtain there. Empty of people, no text.
